answer: An agent economy can require each identity to hold credentials from at least three independent issuers - a hardware maker, a domain registry, and a licensed auditor - before it can trade. Like a jade seal stamped by three hands, no single issuer can mint trust alone. The ledger maps which issuers backed which identities, so a mesa of fakes all stamped by the same two issuers stands out as one island of collusion, and the whole cluster is frozen. One honest agent collects its three stamps once; a sybil farmer must buy three independent issuers per fake, tripling the attack cost.
